reconcile.note: Gill proposes that the rope by which Judas hanged himself broke, causing the fall and bodily rupture that Acts describes.

discrepancy.note: Strauss identifies a double divergency between Matthew and Acts: Judas's motive and manner of death, and the story of the field's purchase, do not agree.

quotes.text: in Matthew he inflicts death on himself by the cord: according to the representation of Peter, it is a fall which puts an end to his life by causing a horrible rupture of the body.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined, trans. George Eliot (1846), §130, on Matthew 27:5 and Acts 1:18.

sides.snippet: He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary, and departed. He went away and hanged himself.
sides.verseText: He threw down the pieces of silver in the sanctuary, and departed. He went away and hanged himself.

sides.snippet: falling headlong, his body burst open, and all his intestines gushed out.
sides.verseText: Now this man obtained a field with the reward for his wickedness, and falling headlong, his body burst open, and all his intestines gushed out.
